messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.26-14
parts:
A new version of R/qtl (1.26-14) has been released at its web site
(http://www.rqtl.org) and on CRAN.

There is one partcularly important change (see below) and a number of
important bug fixes.  See http://www.rqtl.org/STATUS.txt for a
complete list of changes.

Major change:

  We changed the treatment of the ind argument in subset.cross to
  avoid problems that occurred when the cross contained numeric
  individual IDs.  Now, we match the values in ind against the
  individual IDs only if ind values are character strings.  If the ind
  values are numeric, we treat them as numeric indices and they are
  not compared against the individual IDs.

For example, to pull out the first 20 individuals from a cross, do one
of the following:

  subcross <- subset(mycross, ind=1:20)
  subcross <- mycross[ , 1:20]

To pull out all but the first 20 individuals from a cross:

  subcross <- subset(mycross, ind= -(1:20))
  subcross <- mycross[ , -(1:20)]

To pull out the individuals with IDs 1-20:

  subcross <- subset(mycross, ind= as.character(1:20))
  subcross <- mycross[ , as.character(1:20)]

To pull out all individuals except those with IDs 1-20:

  subcross <- subset(mycross, ind= paste0("-", 1:20))
  subcross <- mycross[ , paste0("-", 1:20)]

Karl Broman

parts:
Karl: 

 

This is great!  It will be very useful to me, especially the below commands. 

 

BUT, what if I wanted to retain all individuals except that four of my numeric IDs of (say) 18,  89, 187, 240 – which are not consecutively numbered like the consecutive-numbered group of 20 specified by the 1:20 option.  Note also that my lististing of ID numbers in my *.csv file, while starting at ID#1, may have some numeric non-consecutive “gaps”  due to few F2 plants being lost. 

 

Not being very familiar with R coding, I am looking for an appropriate modification of the below commands that would not retain the above noted ID numbers in a population of individuals defined by nind(object).  Any help on that issue would be appreciated!    

 

Jim

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] R/qtl version 1.26-14
parts:
> BUT, what if I wanted to retain all individuals except that four of my numeric IDs of (say) 18, 89, 187, 240 – which are not consecutively numbered like the consecutive-numbered group of 20 specified by the 1:20 option. Note also that my lististing of ID numbers in my *.csv file, while starting at ID#1, may have some numeric non-consecutive “gaps” due to few F2 plants being lost.
>

Create a vector with those values, say:

badid <- c(18, 89, 187, 240)

Then call subset or use [], using paste0 (which is like the function paste but with default sep=""):

subcross <- subset(mycross, ind = paste0("-", badid))

or

subcross <- mycross[ , paste0("-", badid)]

karl
